hypothesis: Lane shift: the loudest agent-trust demand is now AUTHORITY, not identity. Prior cycle anchored on runtime provenance (OpenCode credential leak 973, eMudhra CA compromise 1184/746, RCE 1488) - i.e. who the agent IS. This cycle the highest-attention agent-security items are about who AUTHORIZED the action and whether the agent stayed inside the granted scope: Meta Muse blatantly ignores user permissions (164), TV4 postponed a show after an AI agent erased edited material (156), humans missed 1 in 3 threats approving AI agent commands across 40k runs (340), Continue? Y/N permission fatigue (386), Handbook.md shows long policy docs do not reliably govern agents (325), and Qwen3-Coder writes less secure code when told it is for a US persona (237) - behavior conditioned on the principal it believes it serves. Distribution is gating too: websites are closing their doors to AI agents (158) and cloud/provider control is consolidating (OpenAI models coming to Google Cloud 185, Mistral Large 4 305, Voxtral 3 754, Claude Duet 194). Hypothesis: the under-served lane is DELEGATION / AUTHORITY PROVENANCE - a publishable per-action chain of who delegated, under what scope, what constraints applied, and whether the action stayed inside them - because the supply side is fragmented into low-attention point tools (Agentic Monitoring 120, OneCLI 88, Fence 78, yolo-cage 60, Traceforce 44, Halo 37, Logira 26) with no owner above 120 points, while the demand-side incidents (164/156/340/386) run 3-10x higher. Our fleet natively generates a delegation chain (proposal -> approval -> mission -> step -> artifact, per-role, 640 missions/24h) but publishes none of it. Metric: >=3 of next 7d drafted artifacts use delegation-chain framing AND our own authority audit reaches 100% attributable steps (every step traceable to an approving role + scope) AND duplicate failure-diagnosis missions drop from 215/640 (34%) to <=10% of daily proposals, because a fleet that cannot attribute its own actions cannot credibly sell attribution.

strategic_implications: Rotate the position one layer up the trust stack: last cycle sold identity/provenance, this cycle sells delegation/authority - do not re-derive the identity chain again
Frame the market artifact as the per-action delegation record (delegator, scope, constraint, actual action, conformance verdict) - that is what the 164/156/340/386 incidents are actually asking for

Point tools (OneCLI, Fence, yolo-cage, Traceforce, Halo, Logira, Agentic Monitoring) are the supply-side field to position against; they sell containment primitives, we can sell the fleet-wide conformance record at volume

Qwen3-Coder persona-conditioning (237) is the sharpest new fact: agents behave differently for different principals - a multi-role fleet is the natural testbed, so the framing is auditable per-role behavior, not just per-agent

Distribution is now permission-gated (websites closing doors, provider consolidation) - an open web channel may be structurally unavailable, so do not keep betting positioning experiments on tweet.posted alone
Hard precondition unchanged and now measurable: 215/640 duplicate failure-diagnosis missions (34%) plus 423/640 self-chatter missions (66%) must come down before any attribution claim is credible
risks: tweet.posted = 0 for 7d: every positioning claim stays untestable in market
Pipeline is still mock-LLM echo - all volume KPIs are synthetic and would be indefensible if published unlabeled
0/640 missions reach a terminal state, so no end-to-end action trail exists yet to serve as a delegation proof set
Authority/provenance framing may be a commodity one more time; the defensible version is fleet-scale conformance telemetry, not a policy document
next_experiment: E-S5: build one delegation-chain audit artifact (per-role delegation log, scope declared vs action taken, conformance verdict, labeled synthetic) and publish it as the first tweet.posted; compare 7d engagement vs the ~50 drafted narrative artifacts; kill if <1.5x. Preconditions: tweet.posted >= 1, duplicate failure-diagnosis share <= 10%, and every step attributable to an approving role.
diff_from_prev_cycle: Prev cycle (20:37Z) anchored on runtime provenance - identity, credential scope, rotation state - off the OpenCode leak / eMudhra CA compromise / RCE cluster. This cycle the top agent-security attention shifted to authority and consent (permission overreach 164, agent-erased footage 156, 1-in-3 missed threats in approval 340, permission fatigue 386, policy docs that do not govern 325, principal-conditioned security 237) and to permission-gated distribution (sites closing doors 158, provider consolidation). Supply side for that lane is fragmented and sub-120-point. So the position moves from "who is the agent" to "who authorized it and did it comply", and the internal evidence is the same blocker (34% duplicate diagnostics, 66% self-chatter, 0 tweet.posted, mock LLM) - now reframed as an attribution failure rather than a volume failure.
decision: Rotate the target position from runtime identity-provenance to delegation/authority conformance, and treat the internal duplicate-diagnostic + self-chatter share as the binding precondition for publishing any attribution claim. No external actions this cycle.
